title: 700,000 People Pack Paris to See the Pope
summary:
Imagine a crowd so big it could fill 10 football stadiums. That's how many people came to see the Pope in Paris on Saturday — about 700,000.

Pope Leo XIV celebrated an open-air Mass at the Place de la Concorde. Before it started, he rode down the famous Champs-Élysées Avenue in his open-topped popemobile, waving to the crowds. He even blessed some children along the way.

In his speech, the Pope had a special message for young people. He called them "today's Church" and praised their "enthusiasm, energy and commitment." He told Catholics not to keep their faith to themselves, but to "let it overflow so that those you meet may be refreshed."

The Mass was attended by many important people, including Brigitte Macron, the wife of France's president, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. President Emmanuel Macron stayed away — not because he didn't want to come, but because France has strict rules separating church and government.

Earlier, the Pope visited a center that helps refugees. He praised the group for inviting people "to see those who are invisible." He also warned about the dangers of artificial intelligence. The Pope's trip to France lasts four days.
why_it_matters: It shows how one leader can bring hundreds of thousands of people together — and how different countries have their own rules about religion and government.

background_read: Pope Leo XIV (the leader of the Catholic Church, which has more than a billion members around the world) visited Paris, the capital city of France.
The Champs-Élysées (a famous wide avenue in Paris) and the Place de la Concorde (a big public square) are two of the city's best-known spots.
France has a rule called laïcité that keeps religion and government separate, which is why the country's president did not attend the religious service.
Article_Structure: WHO: Pope Leo XIV, a crowd of about 700,000 people, Brigitte Macron (the wife of France's president), Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, and the young Catholics the Pope praised.
WHAT: The Pope celebrated an open-air Mass, rode the popemobile, called young people 'today's Church,' visited a refugee center, and warned about artificial intelligence.
WHERE: Paris, France — the Mass at the Place de la Concorde, with the popemobile ride down the Champs-Élysées.
WHY: The four-day trip is meant to encourage Catholics, especially young ones, to share their faith and to notice people who are 'invisible,' like refugees.
